newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks buck Wall St, pulled up by Telmex.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks buck Wall St, pulled up by Telmex.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed up on Tuesday as gains in heavyweight Telmex offset a falling Dow and higher U.S. long bond yields, traders said.
"The market's dead and gains in Telmex, which accounted for one-third of shares traded today, hauled the market up from an earlier slump," a trader said.
The blue-chip IPC index closed the year at 3,361.03 points, 14.08 points or 0.42 percent up on the day, but up 582.56 points or 20.97 percent from the close of 1995.
Volume was a moribund 30.2 million shares traded, due to the absence of foreign players, a trader said.
The Dow Jones plummeted 1.54 percent at 6,448.27 points. Yields on 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds jumped to 6.64 percent from 6.55 percent in late trade Monday.
Telmex L shares closed up eight centavos to 12.98 pesos in Mexico, while its ADRs went against the tide in the New York to gain 1/8 to 33.

Traders noted Telmex stock was in demand by the Inbursa brokerage, which has corporate links to the firm. They thus suspected gains were for year-end valuation purposes rather than betokening any fundamental trend.
